acceptance-criteria.criterion: When tags are posted to an existing link, the system shall attach them and return 200 with the link reporting every attached tag.
When a tag already attached to a link is posted again, the system shall return 200 and leave the tag attached exactly once.
If tags are posted to a link id that does not exist, then the system shall return 404 and create no tag rows.

context.data-model: Tag(id integer pk, name text unique not null) LinkTag(link_id fk Link.id, tag_id fk Tag.id, primary key both)

gaps.gap: Whether a tag with no remaining links is deleted or kept is undecided. Keeping them makes an autocomplete list easy and lets the list rot.

context.prd-excerpt:
Feature "Tag links" (tag-links, should-have).
User story: As someone collecting links, I want to tag what I save and filter by tag, so that a shelf of two hundred links stays usable.
Description: Attach zero or more free-text tags to a link, and filter the list endpoint by tag.
Tags are a separate table with a many-to-many join to links, not a comma-separated string column. This is the one place the fixture deliberately requires a real relationship: a single-table shortcut would make the data-model layer trivial and the fixture would stop exercising the part of layer planning most likely to break.
tag-links declares <depends-on slug="save-link" kind="data"/>. LinkTag.link_id is the foreign key that edge describes.
Considerations (tag-links): Tag names are matched case-sensitively. Case folding is a reasonable product decision but it is not free to verify, and leaving it explicit here stops an implementer inventing either behaviour and calling it correct. This is carried from the feature's <notes><considerations> as an implementation constraint. It is NOT an acceptance criterion, has no criterion id, and must not be given one - the analysis pass recorded that decision explicitly. Its effect on this task: the unique constraint on `Tag.name` is a plain unique constraint over the stored text. Do NOT add a functional index, a COLLATE NOCASE clause, or any lowercasing of the stored value.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- BLOCKING OPEN GAP - the gap itself is carried verbatim in the <gaps> element above. It is `tag-links#1` in gap numbering, which is NOT the same thing as acceptance criterion 1 above; the two numbering spaces are separate.
The gap is UNRESOLVED. Do not resolve it, and do not pick a side while implementing.
The layer plan marks this gap as blocking and records that L4-003 and L3-006 "should not be executed until it is answered". Report that this task carries an unanswered blocking gap before or alongside delivering it.
What the declared model FORCES, and what the gap leaves OPEN. Forced, because the PRD authors declared it: LinkTag.link_id is a foreign key to Link.id and LinkTag.tag_id is a foreign key to Tag.id - both columns and both references are declared, so spell them. Left open by the gap: what happens to a Tag row when its last LinkTag row goes away. That is a deletion policy, not a reference, and NOTHING in the declared model fixes it. So write the FK reference and stop there - no ON DELETE clause of any kind, no cascade, no orphan-cleanup rule, no retention column.
What makes this task safe to write despite the gap: the analysis pass recorded that "no detach or cleanup endpoint and no cascade or retention field was emitted, so the decision does not leak into the merged models or API surface". The models below therefore carry NO ondelete clause, NO cascade= argument and NO retention or is_orphan column. Both answers to the gap remain implementable on top of exactly these tables: - "delete orphans" becomes a cleanup step in a future detach endpoint; - "keep them" is what these tables already do by not deleting anything. Adding `ondelete="CASCADE"` or a `cascade="all, delete-orphan"` relationship would silently decide the open question in the schema. Do not. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

task.objective: Create the two models tag-links owns: `Tag` in app/models/tag.py and the `LinkTag` join table in app/models/link_tag.py, with a composite primary key over (link_id, tag_id) that makes a tag attachable to a link exactly once, and export both from app/models/__init__.py.

requirements.requirement:
Create file `app/models/tag.py` defining exactly one model class, `Tag`:
from sqlalchemy import Integer, Text from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from app.db import Base
class Tag(Base): """A free-text tag. Owned by the tag-links feature."""
__tablename__ = "tags"
id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True) name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=False, unique=True)
The table name is exactly `tags`. L3-004's join and L3-006's handler are written against that string.

`Tag.name` is unique and NOT NULL, matching the declared data model `name text unique not null`. The uniqueness is over the stored text exactly as given: do NOT add `COLLATE NOCASE`, a functional lowercase index, or any normalisation of the value on the way in. tag-links' considerations state that tag names are matched case-sensitively, so `Python` and `python` are two different tags and both must be storable.

Create file `app/models/link_tag.py` defining exactly one model class, `LinkTag`:
from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey, Integer from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from app.db import Base
class LinkTag(Base): """Join table attaching a Tag to a Link. Owned by the tag-links feature."""
__tablename__ = "link_tags"
link_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column( Integer, ForeignKey("links.id"), primary_key=True ) tag_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column( Integer, ForeignKey("tags.id"), primary_key=True )
The table name is exactly `link_tags`.
Both columns carry `primary_key=True`. That is what makes the primary key COMPOSITE over (link_id, tag_id), and the composite key is not a detail - it is the mechanism that satisfies tag-links#2. A second insert of the same pair raises IntegrityError, so a tag cannot be attached to a link twice however many times it is posted. Do NOT add a separate surrogate `id` column: that would let the same pair be inserted repeatedly and would move the idempotency guarantee out of the schema and into handler code that could forget it.

The foreign key targets are the strings `"links.id"` and `"tags.id"` - table names, not class names. `ForeignKey("Link.id")` is a common and silent error: SQLAlchemy resolves the string against table names, so it would fail at create_all time with a NoReferencedTableError.

Carry NO deletion policy. Specifically, on both foreign keys: - do NOT pass `ondelete=` (no CASCADE, no SET NULL, no RESTRICT) - do NOT pass `onupdate=` - do NOT define a `relationship()` with `cascade=` or `passive_deletes=` - do NOT add a retention, is_orphan, or usage-count column to Tag
This is the direct consequence of the unresolved blocking gap carried in <prd-excerpt>. Whether an orphaned tag is deleted or kept is undecided, and any of the above would decide it in the schema. The tables as specified take no position: nothing is auto-deleted, and nothing prevents a future cleanup step from deleting.

Do NOT define any `relationship()` at all - not on Tag, not on LinkTag, and not on Link. L3-004 joins explicitly:
select(Link).join(LinkTag, LinkTag.link_id == Link.id) .join(Tag, Tag.id == LinkTag.tag_id) .where(Tag.name == tag)
and needs no ORM relationship attribute to do so. Adding one would also force a decision about its `cascade` argument, which requirement 5 forbids.

Extend `app/models/__init__.py` so that it reads exactly:
"""SQLAlchemy models.
Importing this package registers every model on Base.metadata, which is what makes Base.metadata.create_all create the tables. app/db.py's init_db() imports this package for exactly that reason. """
from app.models.link import Link from app.models.link_tag import LinkTag from app.models.tag import Tag
__all__ = ["Link", "LinkTag", "Tag"]
Keep the existing `Link` import. Removing it would leave the `links` table uncreated and break every model that references it.
Do NOT modify app/models/link.py, app/db.py, app/main.py, app/api/links.py or any file under app/schemas/, and do not edit any test file created by layer 3.
Do NOT create a migrations directory or introduce a migration tool. Schema creation in this project is `Base.metadata.create_all` and nothing else - the same constraint L4-001 carries.

exports.interface:
# app/models/tag.py from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped from app.db import Base
class Tag(Base): __tablename__ = "tags"
id: Mapped[int] # integer primary key, autoincrement name: Mapped[str] # text NOT NULL, UNIQUE, case-sensitive
# Import either way: # from app.models import Tag # from app.models.tag import Tag # # FOR L3-006: `name` is unique, so "get or create" is the correct pattern for attaching a # tag - SELECT by exact name first, INSERT only if absent. A blind INSERT of an existing # name raises IntegrityError. # # Matching is case-sensitive by decision, carried from tag-links' considerations: # `Tag.name == "python"` and `Tag.name == "Python"` are different tags and both may exist. # Do not apply lower(), ilike() or any case folding in a query or on the way in.

# app/models/link_tag.py from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped from app.db import Base
class LinkTag(Base): __tablename__ = "link_tags"
link_id: Mapped[int] # FK links.id, part of the composite primary key tag_id: Mapped[int] # FK tags.id, part of the composite primary key
# The primary key is COMPOSITE over (link_id, tag_id). There is no surrogate id column. # # FOR L3-006, on tag-links#2 (re-posting an attached tag returns 200, attached once): # inserting a duplicate pair raises sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError. Either check for the # existing row before inserting, or catch IntegrityError and roll back to a savepoint - # both satisfy the criterion. What must NOT happen is the duplicate landing in the table. # # FOR L3-006, on tag-links#4 (unknown link id returns 404, no tag rows created): # the FK to links.id is enforced - app/db.py sets PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON for every # connection - so an insert against a non-existent link raises IntegrityError rather than # succeeding. The handler must still check the link exists and return 404; the FK is the # backstop, not the mechanism for the status code. # # NO deletion policy is declared: no ondelete, no cascade, no relationship. This is # deliberate and load-bearing. tag-links' gap 1 - "whether a tag with no remaining links is # deleted or kept" - is UNRESOLVED and blocking. Adding a cascade would answer it silently. # tests/test_tag_models.py asserts the absence.

# app/models/__init__.py, after this task - final form for this PRD from app.models.link import Link from app.models.link_tag import LinkTag from app.models.tag import Tag
__all__ = ["Link", "LinkTag", "Tag"]
# FOR L4-004: `import app.models` is all a conftest needs to register links, tags and # link_tags on Base.metadata before calling Base.metadata.create_all against a per-test # engine. Importing the three modules individually is unnecessary.
